questions.question: Describe how to construct a 65° angle and how to check that you did not draw 115° by mistake.
questions.expected_answer: Draw an arm and mark the vertex; place the protractor centre on the vertex with the baseline on the arm; mark 65 on the scale starting at 0 on that arm; join. 65° is acute, so the angle must look smaller than a right angle.

questions.question: Explain how to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB with a compass and ruler.
questions.expected_answer: Open the compass to more than half of AB; draw arcs above and below AB from A, then from B with the same opening; join the two crossing points. The line is perpendicular to AB through its midpoint.

questions.question: Describe one method to construct a line parallel to a given line and how to check it.
questions.expected_answer: Construct two perpendiculars to the line, measure equal lengths (e.g. 4 cm) along each and join the ends. Check by measuring that the distance between the lines is equal at two places.
